I'm sorry that’s happening — that sounds stressful. I can help. Quick questions first so I can prioritize options that will get you cash fastest:

- Were all three cards declined at the same ATM/terminal, or at different ATMs?
- Did the ATM show an error message (e.g., “insufficient funds”, “transaction not permitted”, “try another card”)? If so, what did it say exactly?
- Are you in the U.S. or abroad right now?

Immediate things you can try right now (no verification required)
- Try a different ATM (preferably a Rho‑Bank ATM or ATM at a different bank). Some terminals can be flagged (terminal-specific declines).
- If the ATM asked for a purchase + cash-back, try a plain cash withdrawal (some terminals decline cash-back).
- If one of the cards is your daughter’s teen card: those accounts have a $150/day ATM limit, so larger withdrawals will decline.
- Green and Blue cards have daily ATM limits (Green ~ $600, Blue ~ $500). If you attempted an amount above those, that would cause a decline.
- Try inserting the card again and use the chip slot (or try contactless) in case the stripe/chip read failed. Don’t retry many times if the machine reports an error.

If you want me to attempt bank-side help (possible next steps I can take)
- I can request a temporary 24‑hour ATM limit increase for a specific debit card (up to a 50% boost of the current limit) so you can withdraw more immediately. Important notes:
  - Eligibility checks apply (account open and in good standing, account age ≥ 60 days, no overdraft fees in last 30 days, card must be ACTIVE).
  - Third‑party ATM operators may still enforce their own per‑transaction limits that we cannot override.
  - I’ll need to verify your identity before I can act (I’ll ask you to confirm any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, or address). After verifying I’ll log the verification per our policy.

Which would you like to do now?
- I’ll walk you through the immediate troubleshooting above, OR
- I’ll start identity verification and, if eligible, request a temporary ATM limit increase (you’ll need to confirm you want me to proceed).

All three were declined at the same ATM.

The screen just said “transaction declined” or something like that — I don’t remember seeing a specific code.

I’m in the U.S. (Denver).

I’m sorry — that’s stressful. Because all three cards declined at the same ATM, the most likely causes are a problem or flag on that specific terminal (KB: “transaction not permitted to terminal” / Code 58) or a temporary network/outage at the ATM operator. It’s less likely all three unrelated cards would hit card-specific limits at the same time.

Immediate steps you can try right now (fastest):
- Try a different ATM — ideally a Rho‑Bank ATM or one at a different bank branch. Terminal‑specific flags and network issues are often resolved by switching machines.  
- If the ATM offered “cash back” or a combined purchase option, try a plain cash withdrawal only.  
- Try inserting the card in the chip slot or try contactless if available (sometimes the stripe or reader is bad).  
- If the ATM is at a branch, go inside and ask the teller — they can often dispense cash from the teller even if the ATM is having issues.  
- If one card is your daughter’s teen card, note those cards have low ATM limits (~$150/day), so that could explain a decline if you tried more than that. Green and Blue have larger daily ATM limits (Green ~ $600, Blue ~ $500) per our docs.

If you want bank-side help from me
- I can check the status of the cards and the ATM/network if you want me to investigate. To do bank-side actions (look up card statuses, attempt a temporary 24‑hour ATM limit increase), I’ll need to verify your identity first. Verification requires you to correctly confirm any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, or address. After verification I can:
  - Check whether those cards are ACTIVE or flagged, and
  - If eligible, request a temporary ATM limit increase (temporary increases last 24 hours and can raise the limit up to 150% of the current limit). Note eligibility rules: account must be open and in good standing, account must be ≥60 days old, no overdraft fees in last 30 days, and card must be ACTIVE. Also third‑party ATM operators may still impose a per‑transaction limit we cannot override.

What would you like to do now?
- Try the quick troubleshooting suggestions above, or
- I can start verification and then check card statuses and, if possible, request a temporary ATM limit increase for whichever card you want to use. If you want me to proceed, please say which option and which two verification items you’ll provide (DOB, email, phone, or address).

Fine. Let’s do verification and then whichever card you can fix fastest — start with my Green Account card.
